newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen weaker at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen weaker at open.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to trade lower at the open on Friday after a record-setting week. * Traders said expiries of options and futures today will add volatility to the market. *
Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Friday as investors shuffle their accounts after a record-setting week.

"I think we're going to go lower. Europe was lower, the Far East was lower. It's been a good week (and) people square their books (before the weekend)," one trader said. He said the market could be volatile today as options and futures expired. The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index
gained 10.32 points on Thursday to close at 6755.13, its sixth straight record close. The key index also hit a new intraday record of of 6765.09.
The trader said yesterday's gold strength may carry over into today to help the index and banks were expected to improve as rate hike fears remained low.

In economic news, Canada's merchandise trade surplus rose in May to C$2.02 billion from C$1.69 billion in April (revised from C$1.72 billion). Exports to the United States hit a new high at C$20.05 billion, beating April's record of a revised C$19.93 billion.
Overall exports for the month edged down to C$24.49 billion from 24.52 billion, while imports slipped to C$22.48 billion from C$22.83 billion in April.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.2 billion in May, with exports of C$25.1 billion and imports of C$22.9 billion.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Alberta Energy Co Ltd said early today its second-quarter profit jumped to C$1.54 per share compared to C$0.19 per share in the same period a year ago.
* Primex Forest Products Ltd said it turned a C$0.10 per share profit in the quarter, up from a C$0.06 per share loss last year.
